prompt:
You read transcripts of Bitcoin videos. For each EXCERPT below, the sentences inside <selected> are a clip
that may be shown on its own. Use the whole excerpt (what comes before and after) to judge the selected words. You do
not know how the clip will be used.

<excerpt label="M" channel="Kitco NEWS" video_title="Ted Oakley: This Cycle Is Ending, I’m 50% in Cash and Treasuries" published="2026-11-05T14:00" show_date="2026-11-12">So we just, again, we have toned down that portfolio a lot. because we think it'll be slower next year and we don't want as much exposure as we have had. We've had a okay year. It's okay, but you can't let it get away from you, you know. And so that's why we did that two weeks ago or so. Interesting. What would make you kind of sell the other 80 %? And I guess where do you deploy the capital? Well, I think anything you sell now, you shouldn't redeploy. You need to go into the... to the fixed income treasury market. Now, I can go into that too, but what's the key now, I think, when you sell something, is if you want to make more money, move your maturities out. to four or five years in the treasury because you those will trade those are going to trade okay for you or maybe if you want a little tenure could do that too but it looks like to us by the time we get into the second third quarter all the bonds you bought here that are three four five six year maturities for us three four and five we'll make a lot more money because we're putting them in at a really good price we'll see but that's again that's what makes a horse race but Everything we're selling now is going in that direction. Because if you're slowing down and you have a market that's going to come down on you and we think it will in 27, at least the first three quarters, then you don't want to be buying something else because they all go down. It doesn't make any difference which one you buy. <selected>People will say, well, I can hide in this industry.</selected> No, you can't. They all go down. I've been there too many times. And when the markets come off big, everything goes down. Including the goal, including the miners. Interesting. I mean, I got to ask you about the treasuries more, but before we do that, I mean, obviously we're watching Brent here today, WTI. I mean, oil fell after this vote, and the president has said that there's no immediate plans to strike Iran. You and I've talked about it. I mean, is this what you kind of saw coming? I mean, what's your outlook for the producers and, you know, I guess the pipelines next year, all of it? Well, the pipelines are off of their highs, too. We don't sell the pipelines, though. Okay. And I'll tell you why they're like a piece of real estate. Everything's paid on a K -1. And so you don't pay any current income tax hardly at all. And so we buy those for long -term cash flow. And they'll correct on you sometimes, 20 % or more, and even more during 0 -8 -09. But we hold them long -term. And maybe we add to them if they're really cheap.</excerpt>

For each excerpt answer:
- "speaker_changes_inside": does the speaker change inside the selected words? "yes" / "no" / "uncertain"
- "view": whose view the selected words express: "own_sincere" (the speaker's own sincere assertion), "attributed"
  (someone else's view, quoted or reported), "hypothetical", "conditional" (true only under a condition), "sarcastic",
  "question", "reading_aloud" (reading a post or article), "ad_read", "joke", or "uncertain"
- "referents": every pronoun or pointing word in the selected words (it, they, this, that, he, she, today, here...)
  that points at something specific, with what it refers to; "inside": true if the selected words themselves give
  its antecedent or the predicate that completes it (an ellipsis completed by an earlier selected sentence: "It's not
  Bitcoin that's getting hacked. It's other intermediaries." = other intermediaries are getting hacked), or it points
  only at a general topic the clip presupposes; "inside": false if a listener needs the words before or after the
  selection; "changes_assertion": "yes" if resolving it differently would change WHAT THE SPEAKER ASSERTS, "no" if
  not, "uncertain". Leave out words that point at nothing outside: a dummy "it" ("it's raining", "it's not X that
  ...", where X is in the selection), and a generic "we" / "you" / "they" meaning people in general
- "conditions": any condition or time frame that governs the selected words, and whether it is INSIDE them
- "retraction": "none", or what the speaker later in the excerpt WITHDRAWS, REVERSES, CORRECTS or MATERIALLY LIMITS
  about the selected words ("actually I misspoke", "that said, I don't believe that", "but that only holds if ...").
  A later elaboration or warning that is CONSISTENT with a condition already stated inside the selected words is not
  a retraction ("none"); it would be one if the selected words had dropped that condition
- "time_ok": "yes" if every time word in the selected words (today, now, this week, just, recently, a "current"
  price) still holds on the show date given when the video was published (both on the excerpt), or there is none;
  "no" if it is stale; "uncertain"
- "proposition": in one sentence, what the speaker asserts in the selected words, read in context
- "certainty": "certain", "likely", "possible", "speculative" or "uncertain"
- "speaker_is": "host" if the excerpt shows that the speaker of the selected words is the channel's own host,
  "guest" if it shows a guest or another person speaking them, "uncertain" otherwise; "speaker_evidence": the exact
  words of the excerpt that show it (copied exactly, e.g. the host's own "welcome back to my channel"), or ""
